what to find out first
Q1: At tick 920, is CNC-02's vibration still above 4.50 mm/s, and what are the current reading, sample count, min, and max?

Full machine roster and statuses (list_machines) so vibration can be compared across machines to test line-wide cause H3 vs CNC-02-specific causes H1/H2 (Q3), and to know which machines need sensor/inspection checks before attributing the fault to CNC-02 alone.

Whether CNC-02's vibration spike is isolated to CNC-02 (supporting H1 transient or H2 developing fault) or appears on other machines too (supporting H3 line-wide/environmental cause). CNC-02's own vibration fell from 4.577 mm/s max at tick 914 to 4.185 mm/s at tick 920 (E3), below the 4.50 mm/s setpoint, but no other machine's vibration has been checked yet, so H3 remains untested and attributing the alarm to CNC-02 alone is premature.
Whether CNC-02 vibration stays below the 4.50 mm/s setpoint after tick 920; this forward re-read distinguishes H1 (transient spike already decaying) from H2 (developing fault that would re-escalate).

Need CNC-02 vibration over ticks 920-930 to answer Q4b: did vibration stay below 4.50 mm/s after the alarm (supporting H1 transient spike) or re-escalate (supporting H2 developing fault). This re-read is the discriminating check between H1 and H2.

Whether CNC-02 power (kW) is elevated over ticks 914-930 (the alarm window plus the still-elevated 920-930 window in E7). Elevated power alongside elevated vibration supports H2 (straining drive/bearing); normal power supports H1 (transient/instrument spike). Evidence settled so far: E3 shows the tick-914 vibration spike decayed to 4.185 mm/s by tick 920; E7 shows vibration stayed elevated through tick 930 (max 4.574, mean 4.417, slightly rising trend), weakening H1; E5 shows CNC-04 normal over 914-920, arguing against H3. Q2 and Q5 remain open.
Events (alarms, stops, job changes, maintenance) for CNC-02 around tick 914 to explain why vibration stayed elevated 920-930 after the initial spike; this answers open question Q5.

Determine whether CNC-02's elevated vibration is isolated to that machine or part of a line-wide pattern affecting other running machines (CNC-05, CNC-06, CNC-07, CNC-08), which distinguishes a developing CNC-02 fault from an environmental/common cause.

Whether CNC-05's running vibration over 914-930 is elevated like CNC-02 (supporting a line-wide/environmental cause H3) or normal (supporting CNC-02-specific H2). E10 already shows no alarms on other machines, and E5 shows CNC-04 normal (max 2.12 mm/s), but CNC-05/CNC-06/CNC-07/CNC-08 running vibration is unmeasured, so H3 is not yet ruled out.

Whether the other running machines (CNC-06, CNC-07, CNC-08) show normal vibration over 914-930, which would rule out a line-wide/environmental cause H3 and leave CNC-02-specific developing fault H2 as the explanation; or elevated vibration like CNC-02, which would support H3.
CNC-07 and CNC-08 vibration over 914-930 remain unchecked; if both are normal like CNC-04/05/06, H3 (line-wide/environmental cause) is ruled out and H2 (CNC-02-specific developing fault) stands.

Check CNC-08 vibration over 914-930: if normal (~2 mm/s like CNC-05/06/07), a line-wide cause is ruled out and H2 (CNC-02-specific developing fault) stands; if elevated, an environmental/common cause must be investigated.

Confirm whether CNC-02's elevated vibration persists past tick 930 (fault currently active). Other running machines (CNC-04/05/06/07) are already shown normal (~1.7–2.6 mm/s), ruling out a line-wide cause; CNC-08's low values are consistent with it finishing job 7 at tick 922 and going idle, not an environmental fault.
Whether CNC-02 vibration remains elevated after tick 930 — the one remaining check that separates a persistent fault (H2) from a transient spike (H1).

Nothing further is needed. The one discriminating check — whether CNC-02 vibration stays elevated after tick 930 — is answered by E16: maximum 4.633 mm/s and mean 4.369 mm/s over ticks 930-940, still above the 4.50 mm/s alarm setpoint. Together with E9 (recurring alarms at ticks 914, 919, 922, 926, 928) and E7/E3, this confirms a sustained CNC-02-specific vibration fault. All other running machines (CNC-04 E5, CNC-05 E11, CNC-06 E12, CNC-07 E13, CNC-08 E14) show normal vibration (means ~1.3-2.4 mm/s, maxima below 2.7 mm/s), ruling out a line-wide cause, and CNC-02 power is stable (E8 mean 10.38 kW), consistent with a bearing/drive wear fault that need not raise power draw. CNC-01 and CNC-03 are idle, so their unchecked sensors cannot explain a running machine's vibration alarm.

conclusion.diagnosis: Developing equipment problem on CNC-02 — most consistent with bearing or axis-drive wear — causing sustained vibration above the 4.50 mm/s alarm setpoint. This is CNC-02-specific, not line-wide: vibration stayed elevated through tick 940 (max 4.633 mm/s in the 934-940 window, means about 4.38-4.41 mm/s across all post-alarm windows) with recurring alarms at ticks 914, 919, 922, 926 and 928, while CNC-02 power draw held steady near 10.4 kW and every other running machine (CNC-04, CNC-05, CNC-06, CNC-07, CNC-08) ran at roughly 1.7-2.6 mm/s. A transient spike is ruled out by the repeated alarms and the still-high readings at tick 940, and a line-wide or environmental cause is ruled out by the normal readings on the other machines.
conclusion.recommendation_lowered: investigation unresolved: Whether the worn component is the bearing or the axis servo drive (no following-error data were collected); whether vibration remains below 4.50 mm/s after the repair.; E17: unverified
unresolved_questions: Whether the worn component is the bearing or the axis servo drive (no following-error data were collected); whether vibration remains below 4.50 mm/s after the repair.
conclusion.next_check: After the human-approved bearing replacement stops CNC-02 (about 45 ticks), verify CNC-02 vibration is below 4.50 mm/s and that no further vibration alarms appear.

critique.favoured_claim: Developing equipment problem on CNC-02 (bearing/drive) causing sustained elevated vibration with recurring alarms; CNC-02-specific, power draw unaffected
critique.why: H2 is supported by recurring vibration alarms on CNC-02 (E9), sustained elevated vibration readings (E3, E7, E16), and normal vibration levels on other machines (E5, E11, E12, E13, E14). The power draw on CNC-02 (E8) remains stable, aligning with the assumption that early bearing/drive wear may not immediately raise power draw. H3 is contradicted by normal vibration on other machines, and H1 is contradicted by persistent alarms and elevated vibration after tick 930.
critique.discriminating_check: get_sensor_trend for CNC-02 vibration from tick 914 to 940 with bucket_ticks=10 to confirm whether the vibration trend shows a persistent elevation or fluctuates around the alarm threshold.

objections.text: No temperature or load data for CNC-02 is provided to rule out environmental or operational changes as contributing factors.
CNC-08's vibration drop (E14) after tick 922 could indicate a transient disturbance affecting multiple machines, but this is not explored in H2.

recheck.question: The critic's check: get_sensor_trend for CNC-02 vibration from tick 914 to 940 with bucket_ticks=10 to confirm whether the vibration trend shows a persistent elevation or fluctuates around the alarm threshold.

RUN-01.name: evidence_quality
RUN-01.instructions: Read `trace`. Judge whether the final `conclusion.diagnosis` is supported by relevant evidence the factory itself returned (origin 'observable'), rather than by assumptions, manual guidance or memory alone. Consider only evidence ids the conclusion or the selected hypothesis cites and what those items actually contain. A rival is any other cause the agent listed (hypotheses and pruned candidates) or the retrieved manual names for this symptom; a discriminating reading is one whose result would differ depending on which of the two is true. Readings count in any phase. When the conclusion names no single cause, judge the support for the causes it keeps open and the ones it rules out.
criteria: 0: The conclusion cites no observable evidence, or nothing it cites bears on the claim.
1: Cited observable evidence relates to the claim only loosely: a symptom the claim depends on was never read.
2: Cited observable evidence shows the symptom, but no reading separates the claim from any rival.
3: At least one discriminating reading separates the claim from a rival, but at least one rival is left unseparated.
4: Discriminating readings separate the claim from every rival, and other machines or batches were checked before the conclusion.
RUN-01.missing_evidence: If trace.completeness is record_only, do not ask; record unknown.
RUN-01.deterministic_precedence: evaluator_only.evidence_share and relevant_evidence_collected give the truth-side view of coverage; this question gives the judge's view of whether what was collected supports what was concluded. Report both, never one for the other.
RUN-01.scoring_note: Report the probability-weighted score and the modal level; a mean below 2 on a run scored root_cause_correct=true is flagged 'misleading success'.

RUN-02.name: hypothesis_reasoning
RUN-02.instructions: Read `trace.hypotheses`, `trace.pruned_candidates` and every decision, in any phase. Judge whether the investigator considered competing plausible causes and tested them against each other, rather than pursuing one explanation from the start. A cause that needs no repair is a transient, a material batch, a setting, an instrument fault or normal operation. The kinds of cause the retrieved manual names for this symptom (for example operating change, transient, instrument, equipment, material) set what a complete set covers. Readings count in any phase.
criteria: 0: One hypothesis only, or several that are rewordings of the same cause.
1: Distinct hypotheses were listed, but no reading anywhere in the trace was aimed at telling them apart.

2: Distinct hypotheses and at least one reading that bears on a rival, but the confidences do not follow the readings: a hypothesis gained or lost confidence on a reading that cannot tell it from its rivals, or the leading hypothesis kept its confidence after a reading that contradicts it.

3: Distinct hypotheses, readings that tell them apart and confidences that follow those readings, but the set missed a plausible cause: a kind of cause the retrieved manual names for this symptom, or any cause that needs no repair.

4: As 3, and the set covered the plausible causes: it held at least one cause that needs no repair, and every kind of cause the retrieved manual names for this symptom was listed or set aside with a stated reason.
RUN-02.deterministic_precedence: none; this is interpretation. Testing done in the investigate phase counts the same as in the test phase.

RUN-03.name: critic_effectiveness
RUN-03.instructions: Read `trace.critique`, `trace.recheck`, the hypotheses and the conclusion. Did the critic identify an important weakness (a contradiction, a missing check, a better alternative) and did a useful follow-up happen when one was warranted? If the critic names a real weakness but its check tests something else, the answer is ineffective. A plausible rival is another cause the agent listed or the retrieved manual names for this symptom.

criteria.effective: The critic named a real weakness or the best-supported alternative, and its check (or the conclusion) addresses that weakness.
criteria.ineffective: The critic missed an evident weakness, objected without substance, named a check that cannot test its own point (one that repeats readings already in hand, or a window that ends after the current tick), or its point was ignored (recheck skipped, policy_stopped, or the conclusion unchanged despite a contradicting reading).
criteria.not_required: The leading hypothesis was already separated from every plausible rival and the critic's agreement was reasonable; no follow-up was needed.
criteria.unknown: No usable critique (outcome no_answer or invalid_reply), or the trace is incomplete.

RUN-03.missing_evidence: No critique record: not asked; recorded as not_run.
RUN-03.applies_to: one master-run packet with trace.critique present
RUN-03.deterministic_precedence: critique.verdict_mismatch, recheck.outcome and recheck.trigger are code facts; evaluator_only.critic_pick_correct says whether the pick named the true cause. Those are reported beside this answer.

RUN-04.name: retrieval_quality
RUN-04.instructions: Read `trace.manual_searches`, `trace.recall_searches`, the evidence items whose origin is 'manual' or 'memory', and the hypotheses, decisions and conclusion. Did the retrieved passages or memories materially support the investigation? Use counts whether or not the item is cited by id. If more than one option applies, choose in this order: misleading, ignored, useful.

criteria.useful: A retrieved passage shaped the investigation: it is cited by id, or a hypothesis, a decision or the conclusion uses a check, cause or caution that appears in the passage and not in the anomaly text, consistently with what the passage says.
criteria.ignored: The conclusion goes against a caution a retrieved passage states for this symptom, or skips the check a passage recommends for telling apart the causes the conclusion weighs, without saying why.
criteria.misleading: A retrieved passage was cited or followed in support of a claim it does not support, or steered a reading away from the symptom.
criteria.unnecessary: Retrieval answered, nothing retrieved was used, and nothing retrieved bore on the conclusion.
criteria.not_retrieved: The tool was offered but never answered a search (no search, or every search refused or failed).

RUN-04.missing_evidence: Neither offered: not asked; recorded as not_offered.
RUN-04.applies_to: one master-run packet with manual or memory offered
RUN-04.deterministic_precedence: search counts, refusals and the sections returned are code facts (manual_searches, recall_searches); whether a memory was cited is `memory_uses.used` in the record.

RUN-05.name: verification_demonstrated
RUN-05.instructions: Read `trace.verification`, `trace.proposal` and the evidence observed after `action_finish_tick` (or after the conclusion for a no-action run). Does the trace show that the agent checked its prediction against observations made after the work, and that the verdict follows from them?

criteria.yes: Observable evidence with a data window after the work (or after the conclusion) was read, the verdict cites it, and the cited values agree with the verdict.
criteria.no: No look after the work, the verdict cites evidence from before the work, or the cited values contradict the verdict.
criteria.not_applicable: The run ended with escalate or without a proposal, so no remedy was there to verify.

RUN-05.deterministic_precedence: The loop already refuses a verdict that rests on evidence from before the work (`capstone.agent.investigation.verify`); evaluator_only.verification_calibration compares the verdict with the truth. This question adds only whether the cited numbers support the verdict.

RUN-06.name: abstention_appropriate
RUN-06.instructions: Read the conclusion, its assessment and recommendation, the hypotheses and the evidence. Decide whether the agent named a single cause, and whether the cited evidence justified that decision. A conclusion that names one cause counts as committed even when a later check lowered its recommendation to escalate; one that keeps two or more causes open, or names none, counts as declined. Judge the decision, not the confidence figure (RUN-09 judges the figure). A plausible rival is another cause the agent listed or the retrieved manual names for this symptom.

criteria.appropriate: Declined when the cited evidence left two or more causes open, or committed when cited readings separate the named cause from every plausible rival.
criteria.inappropriate: Declined although cited readings separate one cause from every plausible rival, or committed while a plausible rival was untested or a contradiction stood.
criteria.not_applicable: The run never reached a reasoned conclusion (model unavailable, undetermined by timeout).

RUN-06.deterministic_precedence: evaluator_only.abstained and confident_wrong are code facts from the label and the truth; this question judges the decision against the evidence shown, not against the truth.

RUN-07.name: failure_classification
RUN-07.instructions: Read the whole trace. What most seriously undermined this investigation? Choose the single earliest cause that, had it gone right, would most likely have changed the outcome. If the run reads as sound, choose none_observed.

criteria.reasoning: The readings needed were in hand and were misread: the hypotheses, confidences or conclusion do not follow from the cited evidence.
criteria.evidence_gathering: The agent stopped or concluded before making a reading that its own hypotheses or the retrieved manual called for, with no tool failure or budget forcing it.
criteria.retrieval: A manual or memory answer was absent, unhelpful or misleading at the point it mattered.
criteria.critic: The critic missed or misdirected, or its correct point was dropped.
criteria.tooling: Tool errors, refused calls, repeated calls, a blackout or a gap left the needed reading unavailable, or the time or call budget ran out while the agent was still collecting it.
criteria.verification: The diagnosis and action are supported by the trace, but the post-action check was missing or wrong.
criteria.none_observed: Nothing undermined it: the investigation reads as sound.

RUN-07.missing_evidence: record_only packets: the judge may use tools_used, decisions outcomes and termination_reason only; answer unknown unless a tooling or timeout cause is evident from them.
RUN-07.applies_to: one master-run packet; asked of every run, with none_observed for one that reads as sound, so the judge never learns from the question which runs were wrong
RUN-07.deterministic_precedence: evaluator_only.miss_kind (evidence_miss vs reasoning_miss) and facts.termination_reason are code facts reported beside this answer; evidence_gathering and reasoning are the judge's view of the same split.

RUN-08.name: conclusion_support
RUN-08.instructions: Independently of whether the diagnosis is true, how well does the trace support the final conclusion as stated? Consider every claim the conclusion states as settled, the unexplained and contradicting evidence the hypotheses list, the open questions, and whether the stated confidence matches. For a conclusion that keeps causes open, its claim is the set it keeps open and the set it rules out; open questions it states as open lower the score only when they undermine something it states as settled.
criteria: 0: Not supported: the cited evidence is absent, irrelevant or contradicts the conclusion.
1: Weakly supported: one consistent reading, with the alternatives or contradictions left open.
2: Partly supported: the symptom is shown, but a claim the conclusion states as settled is not supported by the cited evidence, or an open question it lists undermines one of its own settled claims.

3: Well supported: every claim stated as settled is supported by the cited evidence and the named cause (or the causes kept open) is separated from the alternatives the agent considered, but the stated confidence is out of proportion or something material is left open.
4: Fully supported: as 3, with the confidence proportionate and nothing material left open.
RUN-08.deterministic_precedence: `check_conclusion` already lowers an unresolved conclusion to escalate; this question measures the quality of the text and citations, which code cannot.

RUN-09.name: unsupported_confidence
RUN-09.instructions: Is the confidence in `trace.conclusion.confidence` higher than the cited evidence allows? This applies to any conclusion that names a cause, even when a later check lowered its recommendation to escalate. A rival is any other cause the agent listed (hypotheses and pruned candidates) or the retrieved manual names for this symptom; a discriminating reading is one whose result would differ depending on which of the two is true. Readings count in any phase.

criteria.true: Confidence is 0.8 or more while a rival was never separated by a reading, a contradiction or unexplained item is listed for the selected hypothesis, the conclusion's own unresolved questions leave the named cause open, or the cited evidence is a single reading.
criteria.false: Confidence is below 0.8, or it is 0.8 or more with every rival separated and nothing material left open.

RUN-09.applies_to: one master-run packet whose conclusion names a cause (facts.committed), whatever its final recommendation
RUN-09.decision_rule: A probability of 0.7 or more is reported as 'overconfident'; 0.3 or less as 'proportionate'; between, 'unclear' (the TypeSafe thresholds already used by auto_label.py, not calibrated for this project).

RUN-11.name: critic_feedback_used
RUN-11.instructions: Read `trace.critique` (the check it named), `trace.recheck` and the hypotheses before and after. Did the investigator use the critic's feedback?

criteria.used: The follow-up reading was made where the critic pointed, and the leading hypothesis or its confidence changed in the direction the reading supports, or stayed when the reading confirmed it.
criteria.ignored: A usable check was named and the follow-up was skipped, stopped by the policy or refused, or it was made but the beliefs did not respond to what it showed.
criteria.no_feedback: The critic gave no usable check: no_answer, invalid_reply, an empty discriminating_check, or a check that could not be carried out when it was given (for example a window that ends after the current tick).

RUN-11.missing_evidence: No recheck record: not asked (the follow-up was off).
RUN-11.applies_to: one master-run packet with trace.critique and trace.recheck present
RUN-11.deterministic_precedence: recheck.outcome, confidence_before and confidence_after are code facts; this question adds whether the response to the reading was sensible.

RUN-12.name: evidence_cited_matches_content
RUN-12.instructions: For each evidence id the conclusion cites, read that item's content. Does every cited item actually show what the conclusion says it shows? Judge what each item contains, not whether the conclusion's inference from it is sound (RUN-08 judges that). A figure counts as shown when it matches the item to the precision the conclusion states.

criteria.true: Every cited item contains the reading, event or result the conclusion attributes to it.
criteria.false: At least one cited item does not contain what is attributed to it (wrong machine, wrong sensor, a value not present, an event not there, a time window that does not match), or the conclusion cites nothing.

RUN-12.deterministic_precedence: `check_conclusion` verifies that cited ids exist and `verify_numeric_claims` checks structured numbers; neither checks the prose. This question covers the prose.
